title: Thread Pool: The Worker Staffing Agency
concept: Creating threads every time is expensive. We need a 'staffing agency' that keeps workers on standby and just hands them tasks.

steps.title: Importing Required Classes
steps.explanation:
**`import java.util.concurrent.*;`**

Importing `ExecutorService` and related classes for managing thread pools.

steps.title: Opening the Staffing Agency (ThreadPool)
steps.explanation:
**`Executors.newFixedThreadPool(3)`**

Sets up an agency with 3 workers on standby.
When tasks come in, these 3 workers take turns handling them.
No need to hire new temp workers (create threads) every time.

**Analogy**: It's like a 'delivery dispatch office' with 3 riders waiting.
When an order (Task) comes in, an available rider immediately heads out.

steps.title: Submitting the First Task
steps.explanation:
The first task (lambda function) is submitted to the thread pool via `execute()`.
One of the waiting threads picks up and executes this task.

steps.title: Submitting the Second Task
steps.explanation:
The second task is submitted next.
Another idle thread immediately picks up this task.
If all threads are busy, this task waits in a queue.

steps.title: Shutting Down the Thread Pool
steps.explanation:
`shutdown()` is called to shut down the thread pool.
No new tasks are accepted, and once all current tasks complete, the threads are safely terminated.
Forgetting this call means the program won't exit.

memoryState.note: Once all tasks finish, the threads are safely destroyed.

quiz.question: Which is NOT a primary reason for using a thread pool?
options: Reducing the cost of creating and destroying threads
Efficient use of resources (memory and CPU)
quiz.explanation:
In fact, failing to properly close a thread pool can keep the process alive indefinitely.
It has no direct relation to shutdown speed.

misconceptions.wrong: More threads always means faster performance.
misconceptions.correct: No! If there are too many threads relative to CPU cores, they spend more time 'deciding who goes first' (context switching) instead of working, making things slower.
misconceptions.why: Thread pools are used to maintain the right number of workers matched to system specifications.

keyTakeaway: ExecutorService is the core of modern Java concurrency programming. Use a pool instead of creating threads directly!
